verdict.rationale: Cursor's first-party docs say cloud agents run in isolated VMs with full development environments, where they build, test, start dev servers, and click through UI flows. They attach screenshot, video, and log artifacts to the PR so the user can review without checking out the branch. Every part of the story (build, test, demo, review) is documented, but only in vendor claims. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration that the end-to-end build/test/demo flow works as described.

support.subject: As an ai-native user, I can have a cloud agent build, test, and demo a feature end-to-end for my review

citations.quote: Agents use their own computers to build, test, and demo features end to end for you to review.
Agents can start dev servers, open the app in a browser, click through UI flows, and verify their changes work before pushing a PR.

Agents create artifacts such as screenshots, videos, and log references to demonstrate their work. These artifacts are attached to the PR so you can quickly validate changes without checking out the branch locally.
cloud agents can build, test, and interact with the changed software. They can also use computers to control the desktop and browser
